clue.text: Rural British superior gripes

parts.note: B is the standard abbreviation for British
U means upper-class, the socially superior usage
gripes are stomach pains, the same thing as colic

explanation.surface: A snooty Briton complains about the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gripes' reads as complaints but is the noun for griping stomach pains. U for upper-class comes from Nancy Mitford's U and non-U usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Bucolic describes the countryside and pastoral life, a literary synonym of rural.

clue.text: Festival period, artist occupying lodgings

parts.note: a month is a period of time, and MAR is March abbreviated

indicators.note: to occupy a place is to sit inside it, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: digs is informal British for rented lodgings
RA, Royal Academician, is the usual crossword artist

explanation.surface: An artist moves into rented rooms for the length of a festival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Period' looks like part of the definition but supplies the month abbreviation; the artist sits inside the lodgings just before their last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Mardi Gras, Shrove Tuesday, is celebrated with carnival parades, most famously in New Orleans, so it names a festival.

clue.text: Unknown picture, essentially, that browser swipes right

indicators.note: to swipe is to grab and take away, so the outer piece takes the others into itself

parts.note: a browser is an animal that feeds on shoots and leaves, such as a deer
X is the algebraic unknown

indicators.note: the essence of something is its core, so only the central letter is kept

parts.note: the central letter of a seven-letter word

explanation.surface: Someone browsing a dating app swipes right on a mystery profile picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Browser' and 'swipes right' suggest a phone app, but the browser is a grazing animal and 'right' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Dexter is the heraldic and Latin-derived word for the right-hand side, the opposite of sinister.

clue.text: Roman here patrols remains, height memorable

indicators.note: a patrol goes round an area, so this piece surrounds what follows

parts.note: hic is Latin for 'here', the word a Roman would use
to remain is to continue to be, in the sense 'is still'
a tor is a rocky hill or peak

explanation.surface: A Roman guards the ruins on a memorable high spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Remains' suggests ruins, but here it is a verb meaning exists or stays. The Latin word splits after its first letter to take the rest inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Something historic is famous or significant in history, so it is worth remembering: memorable.

clue.text: Single soul atop Holiday Inn

parts.note: the soul and the heart are both the seat of feeling
a short holiday is a break
an inn is a place to stay, like a hotel

explanation.surface: A lone guest takes a room at the top of a Holiday Inn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Single' looks like a lone guest or a single room but means a record release; 'Holiday Inn' is split into its two words. In a down entry the soul sits on top.
explanation.definitionFit: Heartbreak Hotel was Elvis Presley's 1956 hit single, so the song title is an example of a single.

clue.text: Annual draw involving tense delay occasionally

indicators.note: to involve something is to include it, so one piece takes another inside

parts.note: a sweep, or sweepstake, is a prize draw
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

indicators.note: something done occasionally happens only now and then, so only every other letter is used

parts.note: the second and fourth letters of the word

explanation.surface: A yearly lottery is held up by nervous delays now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Annual' reads as yearly but is a noun: a plant that lives one season. A sweep is a British office lottery drawn on a big race.
explanation.definitionFit: The sweet pea is a climbing garden flower grown from seed each year, so it is an annual plant.

clue.text: Adult undressed goes to grab ciggy

indicators.note: grabbing something means holding it, so one piece clasps the other
undressing strips off the outer layer, so the outside letters go and the middle stays

parts.note: the word without its first and last letters
fag is British slang for a cigarette

explanation.surface: A grown-up with no clothes on heads off to grab a cigarette.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Adult undressed' tempts you to strip letters from 'Adult', but that word is the definition and the undressing applies to 'goes'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being of age means having reached the legal age of majority, so an adult is someone who is old enough.

clue.text: Sloth inhabiting Scottish county, according to Liverpudlian?

parts.note: something inhabiting a place is in it

indicators.note: what is said according to a Liverpool speaker follows that local accent, so the spelling follows how it is pronounced

parts.note: the county is in south-west Scotland; in a Scouse accent its first vowel comes out like 'er'

explanation.surface: A lazy animal lives in a Scottish county, as a Liverpool speaker would say it.
explanation.walkthrough: Scouse is the Liverpool accent, which pronounces 'air' and 'er' alike, so 'in Ayrshire' comes out as in-ER-sha.
explanation.definitionFit: Sloth as a vice means laziness, and inertia is a tendency to stay inactive, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Fury abandons resistance when power's lacking

indicators.note: to abandon something is to leave it behind, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: fury and outrage are both intense anger
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Anger gives up opposing when it runs out of strength.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Power' and 'resistance' look like a physics pairing in the wordplay, but 'power' belongs to the definition, which is a whole phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: An outage is a period when the electricity supply fails, a time with no power.

clue.text: Found mean American twirling gun very mature

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for American

indicators.note: something twirled is spun round, so the letters are turned to face the other way

parts.note: to gun an engine is to rev it
aged means very old or long matured

explanation.surface: A nasty old American twirls a pistol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean American twirling gun' paints a cowboy, but 'mean' is the statistic and 'gun' is a verb for revving an engine.
explanation.definitionFit: To average a set of numbers is to calculate their arithmetic mean, so averaged means worked out the mean.

clue.text: Listing inhibits commercial vehicle

indicators.note: to inhibit is to hold in or restrain, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: a roster is a list of names, such as a duty rota
a commercial on TV is an advert, or ad

explanation.surface: A tilted lorry, or a rule about commercial vehicles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Commercial vehicle' reads as a van, but the two words split: 'commercial' is wordplay and 'vehicle' the definition. 'Listing' is a noun, not leaning.
explanation.definitionFit: A roadster is an open two-seater sports car, a kind of vehicle.

clue.text: Pop bottles corrode in settlement

indicators.note: to bottle something is to seal it inside, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: to have a pop at something is to try it
acid eats away at metal, so to eat is to corrode

explanation.surface: Fizzy drink bottles rust away in a village.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pop bottles' reads as soft-drink bottles, but 'bottles' is a verb and 'settlement' means an agreement, not a village.
explanation.definitionFit: A treaty is a formal agreement between nations, and a settlement is an agreement ending a dispute.

clue.text: Family bag includes cold seafood

parts.note: your kin are your family

indicators.note: to include something is to take it in, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: to bag something is to grab it
C is the abbreviation for cold on a tap

explanation.surface: A family's cool bag holds chilled seafood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bag' looks like a noun for a cool bag, but it is a verb meaning seize.
explanation.definitionFit: The king crab is a large crab caught for its leg meat, so it is a kind of seafood.

clue.text: Old character's toasty, regularly fixing energy regulator

indicators.note: to fix something is to hold it in place, so one piece holds another inside it

parts.note: rho is a letter of the ancient Greek alphabet, followed by the 's
E is the symbol for energy

indicators.note: taking things at regular intervals means every other letter, starting with the first

parts.note: the first, third and fifth letters

explanation.surface: An old man's toasty home has an energy-saving thermostat fitted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old character' sounds like an elderly person but means a letter of an ancient alphabet; the energy goes inside it after the first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A rheostat is a variable resistor used to control electric current, so it is a kind of regulator.

clue.text: Least familiar path doubled around mountains

indicators.note: going around something means surrounding it, so the outer letters wrap the inner piece

parts.note: ST, short for street, a path through a town, taken twice: once on each side
a range is a chain of mountains

explanation.surface: The road less travelled loops back around the hills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Least familiar path' reads as the road less travelled, but 'path' belongs to the wordplay; the street abbreviation is used once on each side.
explanation.definitionFit: Strange means unfamiliar or unknown, so its superlative means the most unfamiliar of all.

clue.text: Hamburger's fine (figure companion boosted seasoning)

parts.note: a Hamburger here is someone from Hamburg, and the German for yes, meaning fine or OK, is ja

indicators.note: boosting lifts something up, and in a down entry lifting the letters makes them read from bottom to top

parts.note: one is a number, or figure
a pal is a friend or companion

explanation.surface: A burger is fine once the figure-watching friend adds extra spice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hamburger' is not a beef patty but a native of Hamburg, who says ja.
explanation.definitionFit: The jalapeno is a hot Mexican chilli pepper used to flavour food, so it is a seasoning.

clue.text: Son also called, passing most of chicken dish

indicators.note: most of a word is all but its final letter
to pass something is to go beyond it, so these pieces come after the one they pass

parts.note: a chicken is a coward, and a timid person is a mouse
S is the abbreviation for son
aka stands for 'also known as'

explanation.surface: A boy, also named, passes up most of a chicken dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chicken dish' reads as one item, but 'chicken' is wordplay for a timid creature and 'dish' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Moussaka is a Greek baked dish of aubergine and minced meat topped with sauce.

clue.text: Extravagant country seat

parts.note: OTT, over the top, means extravagant or excessive
Oman is a country on the Arabian peninsula

explanation.surface: A lavish country house, or country seat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country seat' is the phrase for a landed family's manor, but here the two words split between wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An ottoman is a low padded seat or footstool, often with storage inside.

clue.text: European embargo restricts huge province

indicators.note: to restrict is to confine, so one piece is held inside another

parts.note: an embargo is an official ban
OS stands for outsize, a clothing size
Northern Ireland is often called the Province, abbreviated NI

explanation.surface: A European trade embargo hampers a large region.
explanation.walkthrough: Northern Ireland is called 'the Province' in British usage, which makes NI a standard abbreviation for province.
explanation.definitionFit: A Bosnian comes from Bosnia and Herzegovina in the Balkans, so is a European by nationality.

clue.text: Sort of court that produces high bounce

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an unofficial mock tribunal that ignores due process
second meaning: an animal that moves by big leaps

explanation.walkthrough: 'Court' and 'high bounce' suggest tennis, but the court is a sham tribunal and the bouncer is an Australian marsupial.
explanation.definitionFit: A kangaroo court is a rigged trial, and the kangaroo itself travels by powerful hopping leaps.

clue.text: Snob Lynn detailed upwardly mobile attire

definitions.note: the answer is a plural noun while attire is a mass noun; clothing words in a mass sense cover several items

indicators.note: de-tailed means with the tail cut off, so each word loses its last letter
moving upward in a down entry means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: the word without its last letter
the name without its last letter

explanation.surface: A social-climbing snob called Lynn is described in her smart clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Detailed' means described in full on the surface but splits as de-tailed; 'upwardly mobile' is a social climber's phrase used for a bottom-to-top reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Nylons are women's stockings made of nylon, an item of clothing and so part of one's attire.

clue.text: Island in south with rich retired sport administrators

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for south

indicators.note: to retire is to withdraw or go back, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: rich food is fat or heavy
the FA, Football Association, runs English football

explanation.surface: Wealthy retired sports officials have an island in the south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rich retired' reads as wealthy pensioners; 'rich' means fatty and 'retired' turns it round. Staffa is a small Hebridean island off Mull, home to Fingal's Cave.
explanation.definitionFit: Staffa is an uninhabited island of the Inner Hebrides, off Scotland's west coast.

clue.text: Fold cloth

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a group of sheep in a pen, or a church congregation
second meaning: a material of wool or cotton waste, or a velvety raised fabric

explanation.walkthrough: 'Fold cloth' sounds like an instruction about laundry, but both words are nouns: a sheepfold and a kind of material.
explanation.definitionFit: A fold is a sheep pen or a body of believers, both called a flock; flock is also a tufted fabric used in wallpaper and upholstery.

clue.text: Cooperative's recruit wearing nothing flash

parts.note: O, the shape of zero, means nothing

indicators.note: whatever is worn is inside the clothing, so this piece sits within the other

parts.note: bling is showy, flashy jewellery
a GI is an American soldier, a recruit

explanation.surface: A new member of a cooperative turns up naked in a flash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cooperative' looks like an organisation, but it is an adjective, and ''s' stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Obliging means willing to help and do favours, which is what a cooperative person is.

clue.text: Forward that is carrying medal over

indicators.note: to carry something is to hold it, so one piece contains the others

parts.note: id est is Latin for 'that is', abbreviated ie
MM is the Military Medal
O is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A forward player wins a medal and makes a song and dance about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That is' is usually IE, but here it is the full Latin phrase; 'Forward' is an adjective, not a player.
explanation.definitionFit: A forward person is bold or presumptuous, lacking modesty, so immodest is a synonym.

clue.text: Car fault reviewed with rest here

indicators.note: to review is to look back over, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: a sin is a moral failing or fault
a san, short for sanatorium, is where invalids rest

explanation.surface: A car's fault is looked at again while the driver takes a break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rest here' is a cryptic pointer to a place for resting; san is short for sanatorium, a British school sickroom.
explanation.definitionFit: Nissan is a Japanese motor manufacturer, so the brand name stands for a car.

clue.text: Bend painting which is sold deceptively

parts.note: a road or river that bends is said to snake
an oil is a painting done in oils

explanation.surface: A crooked painting gets passed off as genuine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bend painting' suggests a forged or crooked picture, but the definition is the whole closing clause, a description rather than a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Snake oil was a fake cure peddled by travelling quacks, so the term means anything sold fraudulently.
